item.description:
Updated 18 March 2026 | Wellness Editor

Things to Do in Balaclava 2026: A Wellness-Focused Guide to Mind, Body & Community

By Nina, Wellness Editor | 18 March 2026

Balaclava isn’t trying to be anything other than what it is: a walkable, slightly gritty, fiercely local patch of Melbourne’s inner south where the pace slows just enough for you to notice your breath. As someone who spends most days interrogating the overlap between physical and mental health, I’ve come to treat the suburb as a living lab. The cafés don’t just serve coffee; they serve community. The studios don’t just teach poses; they teach boundaries. Even the laneway walls seem to exhale a reminder: look after yourself, look after each other. Below are eight stops that turn an afternoon in Balaclava into an intentional act of care—no green juice evangelism required.

Wellness Editor: Nina | 18 March 2026

Prahran still pulses with the same kinetic rhythm that first lured me here a decade ago, yet the suburb keeps re-inventing itself faster than my morning breath-work sequence. In 2026 the change is physical: low-tox refuelling stations, movement labs that double as mental-health sanctuaries, and zero-proof bars pouring adaptogenic nightcaps. Below is the Prahran I’m prescribing to anyone who asks me how to feel stronger, calmer and more connected this year—all anchored to real addresses you can plug into your maps app right now.

South Yarra 2026: A Wellness Editor’s Curated Guide to Moving, Eating and Unwinding Well

South Yarra has always been the postcode where Melbourne’s fitness-first mindset meets its fashion pulse. In 2026 the suburb is doubling down on intentional living: infrared studios sit beside zero-proof bars, rooftop gardens supply the cafés, and every trainer seems to have a psychology degree. Below, I’ve road-tested eight stops that keep my cortisol in check and my step count honest. Lace up, sip slowly, breathe deeply—this is South Yarra, decoded for body and mind.
